answer.evidence: The hood and trunk are drawn as a 10-row textured charred band (rows 9-18) ending in a light red front-edge line at rows 18-19. The cabin roof sits above it as a gray top plane (rows 4-14) with a dark window strip at rows 15-17. Below the line is the body side with door seams (rows 19-23), a dark shadow at rows 23-24, then flat tyres (rows 24-28). That gives a top surface and a front face of 3 or more rows, so it reads as three-quarter.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a wide east-west car wreck with a charred grey roof block, rust-brown body panels and dark tyres. It shows about 5 lightness steps across the rust body and roof, with per-panel highlights and scorch dots. Measured facts: 15 visible tones per tile against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well, and 0% near-flat coverage, so there are no flat fills. Only 17% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines lean brown/rust like the neighbouring material, as in the Beodeul hedge and stall. Total distinct colours (19) are lower than the stall (40) and well (38) because the locked palette is smaller, but the visible tone count is close to theirs. Texture is somewhat less rich than the well, but a careful artist would accept it next to the references without it looking like a flat sticker.
